rows.title: Start dose to kids to max, then across to the other drug

turns.user: I just got put on Lipitor. What dose do people usually start on?
turns.answer:
For adults, Lipitor (atorvastatin) is usually started at **10 or 20 mg once daily**, depending on how much LDL cholesterol reduction is needed. [doc_1]
 If a reduction in LDL cholesterol of **more than 45%** is needed, the starting dose may be **40 mg once daily**. The usual adult dosage range is **10–80 mg once daily**, with a maximum of **80 mg/day**. [doc_1] [doc_2]
 The dose may be adjusted based on lipid results, generally at intervals of **2–4 weeks**. It can be taken at any time of day, with or without food, although evening dosing is preferred in the prescribing information. [doc_2]
 For children aged **10–17 years**, the recommended starting dose is **10 mg/day**, with a maximum recommended dose of **20 mg/day**. [doc_1] [doc_3]
 Follow the dose prescribed by your clinician rather than changing it yourself.

turns.answer:
For **metformin**, safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients **have not been established**. [doc_1]
 Therefore, the provided information does **not support a specific pediatric dose or routine use in children**; a clinician should determine whether metformin is appropriate for an individual child. [doc_1]
 Animal studies did not show teratogenic effects in rats and rabbits at the doses studied, but animal findings do not establish safety in children or humans. [doc_3]

turns.user: And should he take it with food?
turns.answer: Yes. Metformin should be taken with food whenever possible to reduce stomach upset, including nausea and vomiting. [doc_1] Follow the dosing instructions prescribed for you, and contact your healthcare professional if vomiting occurs; the medication may need to be temporarily stopped and restarted cautiously after lactic acidosis has been excluded. [doc_3]
